newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall sharply amid unrest.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall sharply amid unrest.

text.p: Israeli stocks tumbled again Sunday following clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops in which nearly 70 people have been killed.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 4.34 points to 184.28, a decline of 2.30 percent. The Maof 25 index dropped 2.23 percent to 193.08. The declines would be equivalent to a drop of about 135 points on the Dow Jones industrial average from its current levels.
Sunday's closing volume was not available because trading of shares in the Karam index of small cap stocks had not finished yet.
"The events had a very negative impact on investors and most of them are sitting on the fence," said one trader at Bank Leumi.

The Tel Aviv market closed two hours early Sunday and will do so throughout the week due to the Jewish holiday of Sukkot, which celebrates the fall harvest and commemorates the years the Jews spent in the desert during the Exodus. Normal trading hours will resume on Oct. 6.

"We were expecting a correction following Thursday's sharp decline but the market continued to fall. There are rumours that foreign investors started selling today," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Management.
The Mishtanim index lost 4 percent on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend, in response to the violence that has raised concerns about the future of Middle East peace.
Israel's opening of a controversial tunnel near holy sites in Jerusalem last week sparked clashes in which 55 Palestinans and 14 Israeli soldiers have been killed.
Despite declines in the market, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most active share, rose 4.25 percent to 145,462 in heavy trading.
Other active shares included Elite Industries, which lost 0.75 percent to 1,241, and Koor Industries, which fell 3.0 percent to 27,692.
